title: What If You Quit Facebook for a Month?

scenes.text: What if you quit Facebook for a month? Economists ran that experiment on thousands of people.
About twenty-eight hundred users were asked what it would take to leave for four weeks, and a random group actually deactivated.
Those who quit gained about an hour a day offline, mostly spent watching TV and seeing friends and family.
They spent about eight fewer minutes a day on news, and scored lower on a news quiz. They also became less politically polarized.
Happiness and life satisfaction rose slightly and anxiety fell. About nine in ten never reactivated during the month.
The twist: weeks later their mobile use was still about twenty-two percent lower. One month away changed the habit.

description:
What if you quit Facebook for a month?
A Stanford-led experiment paid people to deactivate for four weeks. They gained an hour a day, felt slightly happier, and kept using it less afterwards.
What should we run through next?
